content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make a water rocket, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Attach the nose cone to the main pressure vessel (15 minutes)
Step 2. Research aerodynamic fin designs online (45 minutes)
Step 3. Cut out three plastic fins from a spare bottle (20 minutes)
Step 4. Glue the fins onto the rocket body (30 minutes)
Step 5. Gather tools like scissors, tape, and a drill (10 minutes)
Step 6. Final inspection of the rocket assembly (5 minutes)
Step 7. Buy two 2-liter soda bottles (20 minutes)
Step 8. Set up the launch pad in an open field (15 minutes)
Step 9. Sand the edges of the plastic fins (10 minutes)
Step 10. Drill a hole in a bottle cap for the valve (10 minutes)
Step 11. Sketch the rocket blueprint (30 minutes)
Step 12. Measure the center of gravity (10 minutes)
Step 13. Apply waterproof sealant to the fin joints (1 hour)
Step 14. Insert the tire valve into the bottle cap (15 minutes)
Step 15. Fill the rocket one-third full with water (2 minutes)
Step 16. Decorate the fuselage with stickers (15 minutes)
Step 17. Check the weather forecast for wind (5 minutes)
Step 18. Wrap duct tape around the bottle for reinforcement (10 minutes)
Step 19. Connect the air pump hose to the launch valve (2 minutes)
Step 20. Clear the launch area of bystanders (5 minutes)
Step 21. Pressurize the rocket using a foot pump (3 minutes)
Step 22. Cut a tennis ball in half for the nose weight (5 minutes)
Step 23. Mark the fin placement lines on the bottle (5 minutes)
Step 24. Weigh the rocket components (5 minutes)
Step 25. Mold a small clay ball for the nose cone tip (10 minutes)
Step 26. Clean the surface of the bottles with alcohol (5 minutes)
Step 27. Secure the nose weight with adhesive (10 minutes)
Step 28. Cut the bottom off the second bottle for the fairing (10 minutes)
Step 29. Check the valve seal for air leaks (5 minutes)
Step 30. Place the rocket onto the launch pipe (1 minute)
Step 31. Watch a safety tutorial video (15 minutes)
Step 32. Wash out the soda residue from the bottles (5 minutes)
Step 33. Pull the release cord (2 seconds)
Step 34. Calculate the required launch pressure (10 minutes)
Step 35. Purchase a Schrader tire valve (30 minutes)
Step 36. Lubricate the O-ring on the launcher (2 minutes)
Step 37. Dry the bottles thoroughly (15 minutes)
Step 38. Trim the second bottle to fit as a nose cone (15 minutes)
Step 39. Test the trigger mechanism (2 minutes)
Step 40. Put on safety goggles (30 seconds)
